name: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next Gyro-Coder (agentionai)

lineage.how_derived: 256 of 512 experts kept by evolutionary search over about 2,200 candidate sets, trellis-coded quantization with Hadamard rotation (QTIP family), 2.125 bpw (Coder) or 3.2 bpw (Coder-L)

purpose: Builder states: a 125B-class coding model on a single 24 GB card (RTX 3090/4090, 7900 XTX) or 32 GB card, for local coding help; Gyro-S/M variants for general work.

C++.evidence: KLD 0.118, top-1 94.5 % against Q8_0 (builder, agreement not accuracy)

Rust.evidence: KLD 0.223, top-1 88.7 % against Q8_0, the weakest compiled language in the builder's table; no task accuracy

license.name: Qwen Community License 1.0 (LICENSE file of the Gyro repo is the Qwen text); Gyro format and tools Apache-2.0 per card
license.notes: LICENSE read: grant to "use, copy, modify, merge, publish, distribute, sublicense, sell, deploy, host, fine-tune" with condition 2: a licensee that "conducts a Model as a Service or AI Work Assistant business" needs a separate license from Qwen for commercial use; internal Use that does not make the model or its outputs available to third parties is exempt. Condition 1: model name displayed above 100 M monthly users or USD 20 M monthly revenue. An AI Work Assistant is "an independent AI-powered product primarily designed for AI-assisted coding or office productivity".

architecture.kind: same as Qwen3.8-Flash-Next with half the experts and trellis quantization
architecture.why_this_design: Builder: bring a 125B MoE to one consumer GPU; the n-gram table (50.7 GiB) stays on disk.

variants.format: TQ2_0 (19.92 GiB on GPU, no-PLE file 21.4 GB, full 75.8 GB), TQ3_0 Coder-L (27.54 GiB, 84 GB full)
variants.notes: v1.2 of 2026-10-29 replaced v1.0 and v1.1 under the same file name

pc-12gb.notes: estimate from file size against the budget of docs/hardware (12 GB VRAM with 64 GB RAM); experts beyond VRAM stream from RAM, decode speed depends on that path
pc-12gb.variant: TQ2_0 no-PLE file plus 50.7 GiB table on SSD

pc-16gb.notes: builder targets 24 GB; with 16 GB VRAM about 157 of 256 expert slots would fit (research/08 estimate); table needs fast NVMe

pc-24gb.notes: estimate from file size against the budget of docs/hardware (24 GB VRAM with 96 GB RAM); experts beyond VRAM stream from RAM, decode speed depends on that path
pc-24gb.variant: TQ2_0 no-PLE file plus 50.7 GiB table on SSD

pc-32gb.notes: estimate from file size against the budget of docs/hardware (32 GB VRAM with 128 GB RAM); experts beyond VRAM stream from RAM, decode speed depends on that path
pc-32gb.variant: TQ2_0 no-PLE file plus 50.7 GiB table on SSD

mac-16-24gb.notes: estimate from file size against the budget of docs/hardware (unified memory 16-24 GB, GPU share about 12 GB)
mac-16-24gb.variant: TQ2_0 no-PLE file plus 50.7 GiB table on SSD

mac-32gb.notes: estimate from file size against the budget of docs/hardware (unified 32 GB, GPU share about 22 GB)
mac-32gb.variant: TQ2_0 no-PLE file plus 50.7 GiB table on SSD

mac-64gb+.notes: estimate from file size against the budget of docs/hardware (unified 64 GB, GPU share about 52 GB)
mac-64gb+.variant: TQ2_0 no-PLE file plus 50.7 GiB table on SSD

engine_support.notes: stock llama.cpp, LM Studio and Ollama cannot load it; Tona would need trellis dequant kernels (research/08 effort M)

benchmarks.name: Auto-graded coding tasks
benchmarks.variant: Gyro-Coder TQ2_0 (same experts at 8 bit: 15/16; Coder-L: 13/16)

benchmarks.name: Decode speed on Strix Halo (Vulkan, MTP)
AA Coding Index (aggregator mirror), Qwen3.8-Flash-Next base
benchmarks.variant: base model, not the Gyro quant
benchmarks.harness: aggregator mirror of the Artificial Analysis Coding Index, read 2026-11-19; no per-row dates; upstream AA pages not reachable

strengths: Smaller resident weights than ISTA's Coder (19.9 vs 29.6 GB)
No SWE-bench published but zero tool-call format errors in 292 calls (v1.2)
weaknesses: Needs a fork of llama.cpp; format flagged experimental
General text and knowledge degrade (held-out KLD 0.579)
Bash task 3/10 and four runs hit the 64k limit for Coder-L
Symbol tables weak (Greek letters correct in 2 of 5 runs)
soft.maturity: Small community vendor, format changes between versions (v1.0 to v1.2 within days).

tona_fit.reason: Would raise the expert cache hit rate on the reference GPU (157 instead of 100 slots, estimate) but needs a new quantization format, kernels and has no agent benchmark; compare to ISTA's Coder before any work.

sources.note: page text read through a summarizer (WebFetch)
